summary: Adolphe Retté's own account of what he did to the manuscript of Salomé in Paris in 1891, published in 1903.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote: Three manuscripts of ‘Salomé’ exist, all in Wilde’s hand and all written in French. What appears to be the first draft (MS Bodmer Library, Cologny, Geneva) is lightly corrected in Wilde’s hand only. It is not dated, but is written in a half-leather notebook bearing the ticket of a stationer in the boulevard des Capucines. The presumed second draft (MS Texas), which is dated ‘Paris, November ’91’, is in a similarly ticketed notebook and is lightly corrected in Wilde’s hand. … There may, however, have been still another intermediate version, since two other French writers helped to some extent. The Symbolist poet Adolphe Retté (1863–1910) recorded in his book ‘Le Symbolisme, Anecdotes et Souvenirs’ (1903) that he was asked to remove …
sources.context: Holland and Hart-Davis, in the note to Wilde's letter sending the manuscript of Salomé to [[louys]], on where the play was written and who worked on it. The editors put Retté among the French writers who helped, which is the connection this record rests on; the same note places the composition in Paris in the autumn of 1891, twelve years before Retté wrote it up.
sources.supports: That Retté was one of two French writers who worked on the manuscript of Salomé, and that the work was done in Paris in 1891.
sources.citation_provenance: PDF p. 526, folio 506 read on the page.

sources.quote: les anglicismes trop formels … J'indiquai quelques corrections en marge du drame. Je fis supprimer à Wilde une trop longue énumeration de pierreries mise dans la bouche d'Hérode. De son côté, Merrill lui proposa quelques retouches. Puis Salomé passa entre les mains de Pierre Louÿs qui modifia également quelques phrases. C'est ce texte qui a été imprimé.
sources.translation: the over-formal anglicisms … I marked some corrections in the margin of the drama. I made Wilde cut a too-long enumeration of jewels put into Herod's mouth. For his part, Merrill proposed some retouches. Then Salomé passed into the hands of Pierre Louÿs, who likewise altered some phrases. It is that text which was printed.
sources.context: Adolphe Retté, Le Symbolisme, Anecdotes et Souvenirs (1903), quoted by the editors in their note on the manuscripts of Salomé. His own account, thirteen years after the fact. It names the whole chain of hands the play passed through - Retté, then [[merrill]], then [[louys]] - and all three are now on this map. The editors add that three manuscripts survive, all in Wilde's hand and all in French.
sources.speaker: Adolphe Retté
sources.supports: What Retté actually did to Salomé, in his own words.
